title: Historical V54 - Execution Safety And Gateway Boundaries
summary: How validated actions cross approval gates and reach local or gateway-backed execution.
html:
Historical reference. See the current V55 architecture guide before using this material.

Execution Safety And Gateway Boundaries

Execution starts only after the runtime has a trusted action plan. Trust can come from low-risk read-only checks or from explicit user approval.

Decomposition-driven execution is the default pacing for non-trivial tool requests. Each validated step keeps hard safety in force: blocked commands, deny rules, cwd validation, binding validation, policy checks, and gateway boundaries remain authoritative.

External integrations use the same safety gate even when they do not use the shell gateway. Gmail actions, for example, cross a Gmail service boundary after typed payload validation, account resolution, preview generation, and any required user confirmation.

Safety Gate

flowchart TD A[Validated action] --> B[Classify effect] B --> C{Mutation or elevated risk?} C -->|no| D[Execute] C -->|yes| E[Approval card] E -->|approved| D E -->|rejected| F[Stop]

Gateway Boundary

The gateway owns shell interaction:

  • command execution;
  • terminal sessions;
  • cancellation;
  • working directory markers;
  • platform-specific shell profile;
  • optional managed LLM launcher process routes.

External Service Boundary

Gmail owns mail interaction:

  • OAuth token use;
  • Gmail REST calls;
  • local mail metadata cache;
  • background sync;
  • draft, send, label, archive, trash, spam, read/unread, and unsubscribe operations.

The LLM can propose mail intent and draft text, but it does not receive direct OAuth authority and it does not decide whether a mutation is approved.

Why Captured Output Matters

Captured output gives the runtime evidence for final answers. Detached terminal commands are useful, but they do not produce the same dataflow outputs for later actions.

Minimal reports and staged workflows both use captured output as repair evidence. stdout, stderr, validation failures, and execution failures are streamed to the user and passed back to the LLM only within the configured retry budget.
